novelty_flags.label: conj:gaussian-frontier and conj:gaussian-lower
novelty_flags.one_line: The flagship comparisons to ZhangWangMiao2025 and GleserHwang1987 lack theorem/section/page anchors tying those papers to the claimed rare-shell gaps.

soundness_flags.label: def:score-inversion and the two diameter claims
soundness_flags.one_line: Score inversion can be empty when its positive-denominator test rejects every t, but diam(empty set) is not defined; declare a convention or an explicit nonempty fallback before taking expected diameter.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:score-information / Gaussian-shell conjectures
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Score-information comparability is an imposed observable-law shell condition, not derived for every rare-event law.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The upper and lower frontier is conditional on the LF-compatible Gaussian shell satisfying c_G q_d(P)<=V_d(P)<=C_G q_d(P).

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define the output and diameter convention for an empty score-inversion set, then prove the convention preserves the stated uniform coverage and expected-diameter bound.
Add exact theorem, section, or page anchors for TianWu2025, ZhangWangMiao2025, and GleserHwang1987, stating explicitly why each does not cover the point-identified directional Gaussian shell.

Replace the qualitative score-information justification with primitive, empirically interpretable sufficient conditions and a worked nonconstant shell member; this would make the conditional regime more credible beyond the least-favorable construction.
Sharpen the field contribution by proving or formulating a strict boundary result for learner accuracy, rather than leaving the rare-learning inequalities only as sufficient shell restrictions.

recommended_next_step: Repair the empty-set diameter definition and add precise comparator anchors, then rerun novelty review; the matched rare-shell upper/lower kernel remains field-plausible conditional on its stated shell.
